D010-D005_h001.question:
"It's been a rough stretch. For about two months, I was on top of the world, full of energy. My wife said I was impossible to talk to, just going a mile a minute, and yeah, I probably snapped at her more than I should have. I started buying lots of things, expensive watches, new cars – I just felt like I deserved them. I couldn't sit still, felt like I had to be constantly doing something. But even then, I started feeling… odd. Like the news anchors were talking directly to me, giving me cues about work. I'd feel this crawling sensation, like insects under my skin, even though nothing was there.

That intense period, those two months, it’s mostly gone now. But these other things, the sensations under my skin and the feeling that messages are hidden in everyday events, those have stuck around. It's been five months now, and I’m just numb. Nothing brings me joy anymore. The things I used to love, like playing golf or going out with my wife, it all just feels…flat. Even picking out what to wear for work in the morning feels like an impossible decision. I'm just so drained, and these strange feelings haven't left me, even after the intense energy wore off."
D010-D005_h001.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Inattentive Presentation)
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features

D010-D005_h002.question:
"Doctor, I've been feeling really off lately. For about two months, it was like I was on top of the world – a real whirlwind. I felt invincible, my mind racing with new menu ideas, sometimes working 18-hour days, barking orders at my kitchen staff. My words just tumbled out, sometimes so fast I saw my sous chef struggling to keep up. I’d even blow off steam by driving my sports car way too fast, feeling that rush. My mood would swing from pure exhilaration to snapping at anyone who looked at me funny.

But that’s all gone now. For the past five months, it's just this heavy cloud. I can barely get out of bed, let alone motivate myself to create new dishes. Everything feels foggy, like my brain is wading through mud. The joy of cooking is completely gone. What's even stranger, and it started before all this gloom, I started hearing voices. They whisper my name, tell me secrets about my ex-wife, sometimes they even say she's still madly in love with me, that she’s watching me online, trying to reconnect. These voices, and this belief about her, haven't gone away even now that I'm so down. They're just always there."
D010-D005_h002.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Inattentive Presentation)
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features

D010-D005_h003.question: "Well, I'm a night watchman, and lately, it's been getting harder to do my job. For about five months now, I've felt this unending emptiness inside, like a hollow shell. Nothing interests me anymore. My old hobbies, even things I used to love doing with my late wife, just feel pointless. I can't even decide what to eat for dinner. But before all that, for around two months, everything was... electric. I was bursting with ideas, talking non-stop, bouncing off walls. I felt like I needed to constantly be doing something, always moving, always alert. I went on a few late-night drives, not really caring where I was going, and probably spent more money than I should have. I kept getting these strong feelings that a certain high-profile actress was sending me secret messages, professing her love, and sometimes I'd see her, clear as day, standing in the shadows of the buildings I was guarding. Now, even after that high faded and this emptiness set in, those visions and feeling like she's still trying to reach me, they haven't stopped – they just keep going, on and on, long after I stopped feeling keyed up."
D010-D005_h003.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Inattentive Presentation)
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features

D010-D005_h004.question:
Lately, things have been… off. For the past two months, I've been feeling this incredible burst of energy, like I could run my bakery empire blindfolded. I started investing in three new ovens, signed up for a catering service, and even tried to expand to a second location all at once. I'd be talking a mile a minute, just feeling this overwhelming need to speak, getting agitated and angry if anyone tried to interrupt. My hands would actually hurt from clenching so much. It felt good, in a way, like I was finally performing to my potential.

But then these other things started happening, even before that wild two months, and they’re still here, even though all that manic energy has drained away. I keep feeling this tingly, crawling sensation on my skin, like tiny insects under my clothes, especially at night. And I'm absolutely certain that the new delivery driver, Mark, is madly in love with me; the way he looks at me when he drops off the flour, it's undeniable. Now, for the past five months, I'm just exhausted. I can't find the motivation to do anything, the simplest tasks at the bakery feel impossible, and my mind feels so foggy, like I'm wading through mud. I just keep crying, for no real reason. The feelings of grandeur and endless energy came and went, but these other… sensations and beliefs, they’ve been with me for much longer, and they still haven't left.
D010-D005_h004.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Inattentive Presentation)
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features

D010-D005_h005.question:
It all started about seven months ago. For two months, I was on top of the world. I felt this incredible surge of energy, like I could build a whole fleet of ships by myself. My mind was racing, new ideas popping up constantly, and I just couldn't stop talking – my wife kept telling me to slow down. I was reaching out to old friends, making new ones at work, feeling more sociable than ever. I even got a bit carried away, buying some really expensive equipment for my workshop that we honestly couldn't afford, convinced it was an investment. During this time, there was this woman, a new engineer at the shipyard, who I just *knew* was sending me secret signals, like she was in love with me. And sometimes, I’d taste this metallic tang in my mouth, even when I wasn't eating anything.

But then, that intense high just… deflated. For the past five months, it’s been the complete opposite. I feel so numb, like my emotions are locked away. Everything I used to enjoy, like tinkering with models or going fishing, just seems dull and pointless. My thoughts are foggy, like I’m constantly wading through mud. The strange thing is, even though I don’t have that manic energy anymore, and I feel so down, I still get that metallic taste sometimes, and I still feel that strange connection with the engineer, even though she barely speaks to me. It's confusing because the high lasted for just a short while, but these other strange things are still with me, despite feeling so flat.
D010-D005_h005.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Inattentive Presentation)
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features

D010-D005_h006.question: It’s like my mind has been playing tricks on me for a while now. About two months ago, I started feeling this incredible surge of energy. I was irritable, snapping at my husband and even clients over the smallest things. I couldn't sit still; I'd be up at all hours, redecorating entire rooms on a whim, feeling like I had endless brilliant ideas. My mouth wouldn’t stop either – I’d just talk and talk, barely letting anyone else get a word in. I even convinced myself that a prominent art collector, someone I’d only met briefly, was deeply in love with me; I’d analyze every glance, every email, as a secret message of affection. I also made some really foolish business decisions, pouring money into speculative art deals without really thinking them through. But the really unsettling part is that even though that intense, wired feeling has mostly died down, those strange things I hear and believe haven't gone away. The voices, usually whispering my name or commenting on my thoughts, are still very much with me, even now when I’m not feeling that manic buzz.
D010-D005_h006.options:
A. Schizophrenia
    B. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation)
    C. Bipolar II Disorder
    D. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features

D010-D005_h007.question:
I’m not really sure why I’m here. My husband insisted. Things have been really good lately, actually. For the past two months, I’ve felt… electric. Like I could take on the world. I’ve been so full of ideas for my classroom, redecorating, and even starting a side business. I barely sleep, maybe an hour or two a night, but I wake up feeling completely refreshed and ready to go. I can't stop talking about all my plans and visions, sometimes I think I overwhelm my husband and colleagues, but I just have so much energy and so many thoughts I need to share.

However, I’ve also been a bit distracted by other things. I keep smelling this strange, burning rubber smell, even when no one else does. And I've gotten this really strong feeling that some of the other teachers, especially Sarah from next door, have been talking about me, whispering when I walk by. I even heard them say "she's losing it" the other day, which just isn't true. This feeling has been going on for a while now, even before I started feeling so good two months ago. It's just continued, even as my mood has been up. It makes me really cautious about what I say at school. I also racked up a huge credit card bill gambling online, but it felt right at the time. I was on a winning streak! They just don't understand.
D010-D005_h007.options:
A. Schizophrenia
    B. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation)
    C. Bipolar II Disorder
    D. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features

I’ve seen the way she looks at other guys, and I hear their whispers at night, even though she denies it. These feelings about her, and seeing those figures, that’s been going on for a lot longer than these last two months of feeling so good. The figures and the thoughts about my wife have been with me for a while now, even before this burst of energy.
D010-D005_h009.options:

D010-D005_h010.question:

I barely slept, just felt this compulsion to *do* things, like my body couldn't stand still. My mouth would just run, ideas pouring out, making it hard to let anyone else get a word in. But now, that high feeling is gone, and things are just... strange. I look in the mirror and genuinely believe my organs are slowly turning to jelly, even though the doctors say I'm perfectly healthy. And sometimes, when I'm alone in my studio, I see shadowy figures flitting in my peripheral vision, just out of focus. It's unsettling. This started a little while after that intense period of feeling so high, and it's still going on, even though I don't have all that manic energy anymore. D010-D005_h013.question: Lately, it’s like my mind is a runaway tractor. D010-D005_h016.question:
Doctor, I just don't know what's going on anymore. For about seven months now, I’ve been in a really dark place. I can't seem to stop crying; it's like a faucet that just won't turn off. My classroom used to be my life, but lately, I have absolutely no interest in planning lessons or grading papers. I just lie awake in bed most nights, staring at the ceiling after waking up around 2 AM, and honestly, sometimes I think about how easy it would be to just… end things. I’ve even thought about specific ways I could do it, just to make all this stop.

Before this, for about three weeks, things were different, though. I felt incredible, like I was on top of the world. My mind raced with amazing ideas for lesson plans, and I was working non-stop, emailing parents at 3 AM. I couldn't stop talking, just going on and on; my principal even mentioned it. I was convinced that one of the parents, Mrs. Davies, was head over heels in love with me – she’d wink during conferences, I just knew it. I kept feeling tiny insects crawling on my skin too, but when I’d scratch, there was nothing there. It was all so intense. But that feeling, that high, lasted only a few weeks, almost a flash in the pan compared to how long I've been feeling this terrible sadness. Now, even though the manic feelings are gone, I still have those strange sensations on my skin, and the belief about Mrs. Davies is still incredibly real to me. It's… constant.
D010-D005_h016.options:
A. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Hyperactive/Impulsive Presentation)
    B. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features

D010-D005_h017.question:

D010-D005_h019.question:
It’s been a rough time, doc. About seven months ago, I just started feeling completely dead inside. There was no joy, no pleasure from anything, even my regular construction work felt meaningless. I’d just lie awake for hours at night, hoping I wouldn’t wake up.

Then, about three weeks back, something shifted. I felt this incredible surge of energy, like I could run through walls. My mind was racing, and I couldn’t stop talking, just blurting things out so fast I’m sure nobody could follow. Everything made me angry, and I’d snap at anyone for the smallest thing. It was like the world was ending, too. I kept telling my foreman that the sky was falling and we all needed to prepare for the end. I’d feel bugs crawling all over me all the time, even though I know they weren’t there.

This high lasted for about three weeks, and it was so intense I couldn't even work. But now, that super-charged feeling is gone, completely gone. I’m back to feeling that deep sadness, like the previous seven months, still can’t sleep, and still hoping I don’t wake up. But those crawling sensations, and the feeling that the world is ending, those haven’t stopped. They're still with me, messing with my head even though I'm not feeling all that manic energy anymore.

A. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Hyperactive/Impulsive Presentation)
    B. Persistent Depressive Disorder

D010-D005_h020.question:

I wake up at 3 AM most mornings, just staring at the ceiling, feeling this crushing sadness and absolutely no joy in anything. My COBOL programs, which used to be my life, they just seem meaningless. I've even had thoughts... of just not being here anymore. "I want to die" echoes in my head, though I'd never act on it.

My thoughts raced, and I spoke so fast, I know my colleagues had trouble following me. That’s probably why I’m on leave now. During that time, I remember feeling this crawling sensation on my skin, like tiny insects under my clothes, particularly at night. I remember seeing them, too. But that manic energy, that extreme high, it disappeared after those few weeks.

The crawling, the feeling of something on my skin, that’s still happening now, even through this deep sadness. I still feel like people are watching me, that I have a special purpose, even though I'm just sitting here feeling numb. So that manic episode was brief, just a few weeks in the past, but these other… sensations and beliefs, they’ve just kept going, whether I'm feeling high or like this.
